description:
Strongly-typed Avalonia theming. Decorate a class with [Theme], install this package, and the bundled Roslyn source generator emits one markup extension per public property, so your XAML binds theme values directly with full IntelliSense and no runtime code generation. Extensions sort into {color:...}, {size:...} and {theme:...} by the property's C# type. Breaking change in 1.11.0: color and size tokens moved out of {theme:...}; add the two xmlns and repoint those usages. Breaking change in 1.18.0: the paint namespace is AngelSix.ThemeEngine.Colors (was Colours) and [ColourRamp] is now [ColorRamp].

ACCENTS. {color:AccentBrush} resolves against whichever hue the target control carries, so one accent style block serves every hue instead of a copy per accent. Callers write theme:Accent.Kind="Warning"; the hue inherits down into template parts. Hues and shades are inferred from the theme's own Color Accent{Hue} and Accent{Hue}{Shade}Brush properties, so adding a hue is a theme edit and nothing else.

ACCENT ROLES. [AccentRole] on a property whose constant RampStage value pins a stage generates {color:TextDefault} and {color:TextDefaultBrush}, resolving that stage against the target control's hue — a named token for recurring assignments like outlined text ink, retunable from one property. New in 1.21.0: PinHue pins a role's hue. New in 1.22.0: per-hue policies (BrightStage, ContrastAgainst/Alternate, FocusColour/NeutralHue/FocusSwitch), resolved in the reactive binding. See the README.

ICONS. Mark a class [IconGallery] and every public string property becomes an {icons:IconName} extension. Fixed in 1.23.0: SvgFolder no longer depends on the project path, so a directory containing '#' works.

PREVIEW STATES. theme:Preview.State="Hover" makes a control paint an interaction state without being interacted with, so a gallery or a spec page can show hover, pressed and focused side by side. Pair it with the real pseudo-class in one selector: ^:pointerover, ^[(theme|Preview.State)=Hover]. Being an attached property rather than a style class, an IDE resolves it and a typo is a compile error.

SCOPED REGIONS. theme:ThemeRegion.Theme pins a full alternate theme to a subtree while the rest of the app keeps the global one, and theme:ThemeRegion.IsDark="True" mirrors whichever base is in effect into its dark ramp; both inherit, so a container retints everything beneath it down into template parts, and the sugar degrades gracefully to the unmirrored base when a theme cannot be cloned. Fixed in 1.24.0: the dark twin of an observable theme follows live edits to its base.

STYLE CLASSES. A bundled MSBuild target generates the stub declarations that stop IDEs underlining Classes="accent" on markup that works, keeping them in step with your ControlThemes automatically. Breaking change in 1.13.0: it is now opt-in via GenerateStyleClassDeclarations=true, and the file is generated in full rather than spliced between BEGIN/END markers. Prefer an attached property where you can — a class declared as ^.name inside a ControlTheme is invisible to static analysis, which is the whole reason the stub file has to exist.

DARK SEEDS. [ColorRamp(DarkSeed = "#RRGGBB")] re-points a ramp's dark half at a manual color instead of deriving it from the seed, so a brand color can hold its exact value in dark mode while light keeps stepping off the declared seed.

CANVAS RAMPS (1.19.0). Dark-palette Light stages step towards the canvas, not black; [ColorRamp(InvertRamp = true)] keeps the old direction.

HUE-AWARE RAMPS (1.20.0). [ColorRamp(HueAware = true)] gives stage N one OKLCH lightness in every opted-in hue; see the README.

LIGHT INK ANCHORS (1.24.0). [ColorRamp(LightInk = [...])] declares hand-tuned light Dark stages that follow a live seed edit; see the README.

Bundles AngelSix.ThemeEngine.SourceGen as an analyzer: one install gives you the runtime, generator and build targets.
